final_answer: Ice floats on water due to its unique molecular structure. When water freezes, the molecules arrange themselves into a hexagonal crystalline lattice stabilized by hydrogen bonds. This arrangement creates a more open and less dense structure compared to liquid water, where molecules are closer together. As a result, ice has a lower density than liquid water and floats on its surface. Safe.
